question: The Union Cabinet extended PM-KISAN to 2030-31 with a Rs 3.15 lakh crore outlay. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 Centre–State sharing
It is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% Union funding, paying Rs 6,000/year in three instalments
The annual benefit was raised from Rs 6,000 to Rs 10,000 under the new outlay
It is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development

explanation: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme (100% Union-funded, no State share); benefit stays Rs 6,000/year in three Rs 2,000 instalments via DBT; nodal ministry is Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare.
subject: Current Affairs

question: India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), cleared via a DoT–State MoU this week, is coming up at:

options.text: Sanand, Gujarat
Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh
Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu
Tumakuru, Karnataka

explanation: India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a 350-acre plug-and-play cluster at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh (DoT–MP MoU, Phase-I 100% central funding of Rs 493 crore).
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Cabinet's Rs 36,441-crore expansion of Khelo India introduced two new school-based components and is anchored to two upcoming events. Which pairing is correct?

options.text: KIFS & KIUV; hosting CWG 2030 and bidding for Olympics 2036
KISS & KIST; hosting Asian Games 2030 and Olympics 2032
KIFS & KIUV; hosting Olympics 2036 and bidding for CWG 2038
KIUV & KIST; hosting CWG 2026 and Asian Games 2030

explanation: The Rs 36,441-cr Khelo India expansion added Khelo India Feeder Schools (KIFS) and Khelo India Utkrishta Vidyalayas (KIUV); funding is anchored to hosting CWG 2030 and the Olympics 2036 bid. Nodal ministry: Youth Affairs & Sports.
subject: Current Affairs

question: On the NavIC / IRNSS constellation, consider:
statements: It is designed as a 7-satellite system — 3 in geostationary and 4 in inclined geosynchronous orbit.
A receiver needs a minimum of four satellites because it solves for four unknowns, including its own clock bias.
It offers global coverage comparable to GPS and BeiDou.

options.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: NavIC/IRNSS is a 7-satellite (3 GEO + 4 GSO) *regional* system covering India + ~1,500 km beyond — not global (statement 3 wrong). Four satellites are needed to solve x, y, z and receiver clock bias.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Match India's maritime doctrine ladder with its year of articulation:

options.text: 1-ii, 2-iii, 3-i
1-i, 2-ii, 3-iii
1-iii, 2-i, 3-ii
1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii

explanation: SAGAR (2015) → MAHASAGAR (2025) → SHANTI (2026), the last being the operational norms-based maritime governance framework piloted in the Bay of Bengal.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Supreme Court this week quashed the 2021 Office Memorandum on ex post facto (retrospective) environmental clearances, holding that:

options.text: All retrospective clearances are permanently and absolutely barred
Prior EC under the EIA Notification 2006 is mandatory, and any amnesty must come via statutory notification under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — not an administrative order
The power to grant retrospective clearances lies solely with the National Green Tribunal
The 2021 OM was upheld as a valid exercise of executive discretion

explanation: The Court held prior EC under the EIA Notification 2006 is mandatory; any retrospective amnesty needs a statutory notification under Section 3 of the EP Act, 1986, not an OM. It allowed only a narrow, time-bound, supervised window — not an absolute bar (so (a) is wrong).
subject: Current Affairs

question: 'Samudra Manthan', the Rs 84,084-crore scheme cleared this week, is a Central Sector Scheme of which ministry, for what purpose?

options.text: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways — port modernisation
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas — deepwater and ultra-deepwater oil & gas exploration
Ministry of Earth Sciences — deep-ocean mineral mining
Ministry of Fisheries — offshore aquaculture

explanation: 'Samudra Manthan' is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (Rs 84,084 cr to FY2030-31) for deepwater/ultra-deepwater oil & gas exploration; targets >600 MMTOE reserve accretion.
subject: Current Affairs

question: On the ILO Convention No. 193 ("Decent Work in the Platform Economy"), adopted this week, consider:
statements: It is the first legally binding international labour standard specific to the platform/gig economy.
The ILO is the only tripartite agency of the UN.

options.text: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: C-193 is the first binding standard for the platform economy, and the ILO is the only tripartite UN agency. India abstained (it did not vote against) — so statement 2 is wrong.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Centre front-loaded Rs 1,09,019 crore of tax devolution to States this week — the first year of the 16th Finance Commission award period. Which is correct?

options.text: The 16th FC is chaired by N.K. Singh; vertical share raised to 50%
The 16th FC is chaired by Arvind Panagariya; vertical share retained at 41%; award period 2026–31
Devolution is tied money that States must spend on capex
The award period is 2025–30 with a 42% vertical share

explanation: The 16th FC (Arvind Panagariya), award period 2026–31, kept the vertical share at 41%; devolution is untied money, so (c) is wrong.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY) approved this week targets ~5,000 MW of capacity. Its defining design feature is:

options.text: Rooftop solar with net metering on government buildings
Floating Solar PV (FSPV) co-located with mandatory energy storage, under MNRE
Ground-mounted solar parks in desert regions
Concentrated solar thermal with molten-salt storage

explanation: PM-SSY (Rs 5,070 cr, MNRE) builds Floating Solar PV with mandatory energy storage (≥2 hours) — a land-neutral, grid-firming design, not plain capacity.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Glaw Lake, designated this week, is notable because it is:

options.text: India's 101st Ramsar Site and Arunachal Pradesh's first, lying inside the Kamlang Tiger Reserve
India's 75th Ramsar Site and Assam's first
A newly declared biosphere reserve in Sikkim
India's largest freshwater lake, in Manipur

explanation: Glaw Lake (Lohit district) is India's 101st Ramsar Site and Arunachal Pradesh's first, lying inside the Kamlang Tiger Reserve.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Which of the following did India do this week? Consider:
statements: Signed two INR-denominated Lines of Credit with Sri Lanka (railways and livestock).
The Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2026 ranked India 176th of 177.
The Pacific nation Nauru formally became the Republic of Naoero.

options.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: All three occurred this week: the two INR LoCs to Sri Lanka (USD 250 mn railways + USD 100 mn livestock), EPI 2026 ranking India 176/177, and Nauru becoming the Republic of Naoero.
subject: Current Affairs

question: India has how many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and which ministry runs the scheme for their development?

options.text: 52 PVTGs; Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
75 PVTGs; Ministry of Tribal Affairs
705 PVTGs; Ministry of Rural Development
89 PVTGs; Ministry of Home Affairs

explanation: There are 75 PVTGs (of 705 Scheduled Tribes), and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs runs the Development of PVTGs scheme. First identified in 1975 (52) + 1993 (23).
subject: Society

question: The concept of Sanskritisation — a lower caste emulating the customs of a higher caste to raise its social status — was coined by:

options.text: G.S. Ghurye
B.R. Ambedkar
M.N. Srinivas
André Béteille

explanation: M.N. Srinivas coined *Sanskritisation* (and also the "dominant caste" and "Westernisation" concepts).
subject: Society

question: According to NFHS-5 (2019-21), the all-India sex ratio (females per 1000 males) for the total population:

options.text: Fell below 940 for the first time
Crossed 1000 for the first time, reaching 1020
Remained unchanged from NFHS-4 at 991
Was 943, matching the 2011 Census

explanation: NFHS-5 recorded an all-India sex ratio of 1020 females per 1000 males — the first time it crossed 1000 (up from 991 in NFHS-4). Note: this is the *total-population* ratio, not sex ratio at birth.
subject: Society

question: In Indian sociology, the "dominant caste" (a caste that wields decisive economic and political power in a village) is a concept associated with:

options.text: Louis Dumont
M.N. Srinivas
Irawati Karve
David Hardiman

explanation: The "dominant caste" concept is M.N. Srinivas's, from his study of Rampura village, Karnataka.
subject: Society

question: The demographic dividend refers to:

options.text: A rise in per-capita income caused solely by rural-to-urban migration
The growth potential from a rising share of working-age population (15–64) relative to dependents
The dividend paid by public-sector firms from population-linked schemes
The fall in total fertility rate below replacement level

explanation: The demographic dividend is the growth potential from a rising share of the working-age population (15–64) relative to dependents.
subject: Society

question: Consider the following on India's Scheduled Tribes:
statements: The President specifies STs for a State/UT under Article 342, in consultation with the Governor.
There is a single national list of Scheduled Tribes applicable uniformly across all States.
"Tribe" is not defined anywhere in the Constitution.

options.text: 1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: Article 342 lets the President specify STs in consultation with the Governor (1 correct); the Constitution does not define "tribe" (3 correct). Lists are State-specific, not a single uniform national list (2 wrong).
subject: Society

question: Replacement-level fertility — the Total Fertility Rate at which a population exactly replaces itself from one generation to the next — is conventionally taken as:
explanation: Replacement-level fertility is a TFR of 2.1. (India's TFR is now below this, ~2.0.)
subject: Society

question: The distinction between communalism and communitarianism / secularism is a recurring Society theme. Which statement best captures the Indian constitutional model of secularism?

options.text: Strict separation of religion and state, with the state having no engagement with any religion (the "wall of separation")
"Principled distance" — the state may engage with religion, intervening or abstaining to promote equality, liberty and social reform
A theocratic state privileging the majority religion
The state must fund all religions equally in proportion to their population

explanation: India follows "principled distance" (Rajeev Bhargava's term) — the state may engage with or distance itself from religion to advance equality, liberty and reform — not the strict "wall of separation" (a).
